hardspace-shipbreaker game sourced

Hardspace: Shipbreaker

A zero-gravity salvage sim in which the player cuts derelict ships apart with a laser cutter and grapple, manages decompression and volatile systems, and sorts salvage to pay down a large debt.

2020Blackbird InteractiveJob simcluster c157 mechanics
this record asyaml sourcemarkdownjson

core loop

start a shift -> scan the ship -> vent pressure and make power, fuel, coolant, and reactor systems safe -> cut parts free -> grapple them to the correct receptacle -> salvage value pays down debt -> buy tool upgrades

design notes

Each ship is a physics assembly of joined parts and typed hazards rather than an authored level: cutting into a pressurized room causes explosive decompression, cutting live electrical wires or coolant pipes can explode, and a reactor removed from its casing must be delivered before it melts down. The order of disassembly is the puzzle, and the taxonomy lacks a mechanic for it (proposed as salvage-deconstruction). Oxygen and thruster fuel act as survival stocks, and shifts are timed except in Open Shift mode.

relations

7 stored edges
uses

Rigid-body physics

Ships are assemblies of separable parts; freed parts keep mass and momentum in zero gravity and are pulled or flung with the tether grapple toward the right receptacle.

core
uses

Surface work tools

The laser cutter severs structure at cut points and joints; cutting live electrical wires or coolant pipes can cause an explosion, so where and in what order to cut is the core decision.

core
uses

Daily action budget

Shifts are timed; Open Shift mode removes the limit.

supporting
uses

Fluid and gas simulation

Rooms hold atmosphere, and an uncontrolled decompression flushes the player and loose objects out of the ship.

supporting
uses

Loans and debt

The character owes $1.2 billion to Lynx Corporation, and salvage earnings pay it down.

supporting
uses

Procedural checklists

Systems must be made safe in order: pressurized rooms vented, electrical and coolant lines avoided, and reactors delivered before they melt down; mistakes produce the physical result rather than an error.

supporting
uses

Survival meters

Oxygen and thruster fuel deplete during a shift and must be replenished.
